subject: tattoo needle skin
title: What If You Got a Tattoo? Your Body Never Stops Fighting It

scenes.text: What if you got a tattoo? Your body starts a fight it can never win.
The needle drives ink a millimeter or two deep, into the dermis, up to thousands of times a minute.
In the first weeks of healing, roughly a third of the ink flakes away with the top layer of skin.
The rest gets swallowed by immune cells called macrophages. They can't digest it, so they just hold it.
When those cells die, new ones swallow the same ink. Tiny particles even travel to your lymph nodes.
So your tattoo isn't really in your skin. It's held hostage by your immune system, passed cell to cell.

description:
What if you got a tattoo? Ink goes into the dermis, immune cells called macrophages swallow it, and when they die new ones re-capture the same ink (a 2018 mouse study).
Nanoparticles of pigment also reach the lymph nodes, which can turn the colour of the tattoo (2017 synchrotron study).
